doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Live Lookout Farm at Keystone Korner and The Last Call
summary: A&M let him record live at Keystone Korner; The Last Call featured his young San Francisco group and was released only around 1981.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: There’s a variety of things with – at least the Forgotten Fantasies date we talked about. Then there’s the Lookout Farm date that Mosaic Select put out in recent years, that was done in San Francisco.

It wasn’t – it was a date. That was A&M. It was, again, John just letting me do what I wanted to. “John, can I record live?” “Sure, Dave.” John was very generous. Somewhere in the ’80s, he had all the reels. He said, you can have them. I transferred everything.
Now, here’s your first quintet date, with Mark Isham and Mike Formanek and . . .
Yeah. That’s my trying to get back into – that is that bad period, ’80, ’81.

Yeah, but that’s released – I didn’t release it until ’80, ’81. That was the San Francisco M, M, and M group I was talking about. I had the tape. Finally, in ’81, I found Joe Haider and had to get a record out and so on. But that was done during the San Francisco time.
